chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ṣafwān, from Ibn Bukayr, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about flour with which one performs washing; he said: “There is no harm in washing with it and benefiting from it.”

So its meaning is that wiping with it is permissible, and the washing meant here is that which is for cleanliness and beautification, not the wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer), and that which makes this clear.

key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), specifically the ritual ablution for salat (prayer)
key_terms.يُتَوَضَّأُ: to perform washing or wudu (ablution), here discussed in a qualified sense
key_terms.يُنْتَفَعَ: to derive benefit or make use of

ai.seo_question: Can flour be used for wudu (ablution) or only for wiping and general cleansing?
ai.summary: This report discusses the use of flour in relation to washing and clarifies that there is no harm in benefiting from it in that way. The concluding explanation states that this refers to wiping or cleansing for cleanliness, not wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer).
